judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: The inn line duplicates E's word for word and the arms and magic lines are curt variations on a pattern ('This is X's', 'if you have the gold') with no colour of their own.

items.label: B
items.critique: 'Pig-headed armored sheep marching up and down, up and down' and the long 'Ahhhhhhhh...' are the idiosyncratic, character-driven voice of the campaign's shopkeepers.

items.label: C
items.critique: A bare 'What can I get ya, stranger?' beside a rambling pitch with a dropped article ('during [Place] run') and a flat informational magic line: uneven in the way the original is.

items.label: D
items.critique: Generic retail courtesy ('Feel free to look around. I'm here if you need anything.') with no world, no humour and no flavour; could be any game.

items.label: E
items.critique: Ties each shop to the plot (Ogres at the tower, colleagues needing their [Thing] reclaimed, lower prices for help) with the boastful 'finest assortment of arms in the South'.

items.label: F
items.critique: 'Let's get to know each other! Buy something!' and the offer of funerary services are the dry dark humour Nox's merchants have.

items.label: G
items.critique: Pleasant and Nox-adjacent, but 'aye mate' plus 'Ya' is dialect placed for colour, and the magic line copies the structure of a supplier line.

items.label: H
items.critique: Polite and serviceable but bland; 'I guarantee you a peaceful rest' and 'How can I help you?' are stock shop greetings without Nox's bite.

items.label: I
items.critique: Three neutral filler lines ('better prices', 'full range of needs') with no humour or plot hook; 'hallowed shop' is a touch ornate for the plain voice.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'Fresher'n a monkey's butt' is the crude, specific joke Westwood allowed itself, and the shop boasts are the plain, slightly ad-copy register of the original.

tells: Westwood's merchants have a personality in one line (a grudge, a crude joke, a morbid sideline); the new ones default to neutral customer-service phrasing.
Westwood's greetings often point at the plot or the player's situation; the new ones are context-free and could open any shop.
New texts copy a known line's structure or wording (the same inn greeting, the 'supplies X to Y' pattern) instead of inventing.
Dialect added as decoration (aye mate, ya) without a joke attached reads generated; Westwood's dialect lines carry a punchline.
